phaseInheritance: All Phase 1 tests remain in active testing and run under `pnpm test`.

features.notes: Asserts the 73-key model with 43 white and 30 black keys and the E-to-E range.
Asserts the six ordered hardware sections and that their normalized width fractions sum to 1.
Asserts the section/control inventory and that only Program and Synth own primary OLED displays (Organ, Piano, Effects do not).
Asserts the keyboard key model (counts, ratio, black-key height fraction) used for pressed/released state.
Covered by the hardware-model suite (section/control inventory and display-location assertions that back button/LED state).
Asserts knob/encoder controls carry numeric value plus min/max and that the value stays within range (clamping intent).
Asserts every control has a non-empty label and a valid type for role mapping.
Asserts the ordered section layout (performance first) backing a continuous chassis with no extra region above the instrument.
Exercises note-on records an active note, note-off removes it, repeated note-on on one source replaces the prior note, independent sources tracked separately, and all-notes-off clears every source.
Real InputHandler + NoteLifecycleService: spacebar drives sustain pedal down/up transitions and MIDI CC64 (>=64 down, <64 up, boundary at 64) toggles the sustain state.
Exercises voice allocation with unique IDs, voice counting, deterministic LRU/FIFO and velocity-weighted stealing at capacity, release marking, and reset/cleanup.
Touch-curve velocity transformation (heavy boosts, light attenuates, medium preserves) and 0-1 normalization, plus real MIDI note-on velocity scaling (value/127) through InputHandler.

Real InputHandler: QWERTY keys map to correct MIDI notes, keyup releases, OS auto-repeat keydown does NOT retrigger a held note, Escape/all-notes-off clears active notes, and detach removes window listeners (blur cleanup).

Real InputHandler MIDI path: note-on triggers a note with velocity scaled to value/127, note-off (0x80 and velocity-0 note-on) releases, sustain CC64 sets sustain, and disconnected/permission-denied requestMIDIAccess resolve to a safe no-op teardown without throwing.

Master volume and reverb-wet parameter changes are clamped to 0-1, and the real Web Audio boundary (gain-node attenuation and convolver-based reverb) is validated where OfflineAudioContext is available.

Real AudioContextProvider + PianoEngine: with no window.AudioContext, create() still yields a usable not-running provider; getContext()/initialize() surface a labeled 'AudioContext not available' error; a throwing constructor is surfaced; and the engine constructs and its API stays callable (playable) in the degraded/fallback state.
The inherited Phase 1 suite (hardware model, keyboard model, accessibility controls) remains present and green under `pnpm test`.
